chunks: 5. My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him: 'What do you think of what has happened and what will happen until the Day of Resurrection? Is it not in the Knowledge of Allah?' He said: 'Yes, before He created the heavens and the earth.'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about Allah's knowledge of past and future events?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the eternal nature of divine knowledge by confirming that all past and future events were known to Allah before the creation of the heavens and the earth. This establishes the foundation for the Shia doctrine of *Ilm al-Ghayb* (Knowledge of the Unseen), distinguishing between God's absolute, pre-eternal knowledge and the temporal unfolding of creation, thereby supporting the concept of *Jabr* (divine decree) within the framework of *al-Amr bayn al-Amrayn*.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 5. My father (RA) that Sa`d ibn `Abd Allah, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Hisham, on the authority of Ibn Abu `Umayr, on the authority of Mansur ibn Hazim, that

I asked Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) “Do you know everything that has happened and everything that will happen until the Day of Judgement? Is it not part of Allah’s knowledge?” He (AS) answered: “It is certainly part of Allah’s Knowledge. He knew everything before He created the Heavens and the Earth.”
